1.why: Text renders in a clean sans-serif with comfortable line spacing on all screens, though letter spacing is default rather than notably generous and the small monospace Logs box is less readable.

2.why: No italics, all-caps strings, or dense paragraphs appear anywhere; headings, labels, and buttons all use short title- or sentence-case text.

3.why: The single-column, mobile-width layout is readable and well ordered, but the dark Logs panel overflows the card's edges on every screen, slightly breaking the layout.

4.why: Instructions are one or two short plain sentences (e.g., 'Confirm your account details before setting up payment security'), with only 'placeholders' as mild jargon in the demo note.

5.why: Both fields show example values (marcus@example.com, +15551234567) as placeholders, but these examples disappear once the user starts typing and no example is shown for any later code entry.

6.why: No screen requires reading a long block of text; the longest content is a single-sentence instruction or error banner.

7.why: No OTP or recovery codes are ever presented in copyable form — the flow never advances beyond sign-in and even the demo credentials must be typed by hand.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent alternative to manual entry appears on any screen; the authenticator setup introduction never loads.

9.why: The email and phone fields are standard inputs that browsers may autofill, but there is no visible autocomplete support, no password field, and no one-time-code entry, so autofill/password-manager support cannot be confirmed.

10.why: The large blue Continue button (with a visible focus ring) stands out, but there is no step or progress indicator and screens 3-4 repeat the sign-in view with a stale error, leaving the user's position in the enrolment unclear.

11.why: Each screen requests a single primary action via one Continue button, with no competing calls to action.

12.why: After submitting, the only feedback is the generic banner 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.', which persists unchanged on later screens and never states what happened or what comes next on success.

13.why: The user can retry by pressing Continue again with no visible penalty, but no reveal/hide or re-request controls for codes exist because code entry is never reached.

14.why: The error banner avoids blaming the user but is generic — it neither states what the problem was nor how to fix it, even when the correct demo credentials are entered.

15.why: No countdown, expiry, or reading time limit appears on any screen, though generous time for code entry cannot be confirmed because OTP entry is never reached.
